challenged_assumptions: BC-1 'Residual: none' premature. Redesigned Phase 3 (engine as extra applicationMessage listener; compare buildProjection(engineLog) vs legacy stateRef.current) tests ONLY projection-layer accuracy — both sides receive identical callbacks from the same EventEmitter (device-sync.ts:891, task-store.tsx:255). Divergence can only surface AcceptedDomainEvent wrapping / idempotency-key errors, not state-machine behavior. The engine's joining gate, live-cutover buffering, deferred retry, epoch-gating are INACTIVE in Phase 3 (listener-only mode). In Phase 5 the engine owns ingest and drives the state machine; bugs there produce NO signal in Phase 3. Phase 3 validates the already-proven projection (task-reducer.ts:5-105) and leaves the novel middle shell unvalidated until Phase 5 activates it.

Invariant 3 'same-epoch only' does not satisfy P4 (spec.md:129 'recovery equivalent by design') for the motivating event class. Any commit that advances epoch while unreadable events are parked creates cross-epoch deferred events — a normal condition. On restart, deferred-store has the ids and raw-log has ciphertext, but the epoch-N ratchet key is gone: documented irrecoverable loss, not equivalent recovery. Worse, spec.md:663 STILL states the full unqualified Invariant 3. Stories written from spec.md will implement the full invariant; the weakening lives only in the proposal — a spec-implementation mismatch on day one.

CA-3 own-echo 'test-cover' does not gate THIS repo. Fork tests live in /tmp/marmot-ts and run in fork CI; CLAUDE.md says this repo consumes a packed tarball (clone->build->pack->npm install). Fork-resident tests are not executed here — only the artifact is consumed. A fork own-echo change fails fork CI but does not block this repo's merges. The engine property test would catch a double-apply only if CI constructs a self-echo-through-engine scenario — an unspecified, non-trivial harness. Detection depends entirely on fork CI discipline.
paradigm_risks: No formal FSM transition table. Nine states named (uninitialized/joining/recovering/catching_up/buffering_live/live/degraded/retrying_deferred/stopped) but legal transitions, entry/exit conditions, and degraded-as-orthogonal-health are unspecified. Three story authors implementing receive-engine.ts will agree on state names but not on transition semantics — producing partially-incompatible state machines.

marmot-adapter.ts 'all coupling contained here' (ET-1) contradicts the module map: receive-engine.ts absorbs ingestGroupEventsRaw (device-sync.ts:677-761) and syncGroup (895-1010), both of which call group.ingest() (700) and client.network.subscription() (942) directly. If the engine absorbs these verbatim, src/engine imports marmot-ts types and ET-1 is false. If the adapter mediates, the engine<->adapter interface is unspecified. The proposal holds both claims at once without resolving the seam.
replaceability_gaps: buildProjection fold order over the mixed-sourceKind log is unspecified. The log mixes bootstrap-sourced events (id bootstrap:..., earlier acceptedAt) and MLS-sourced (id rumor.id, later acceptedAt). FWW for task.created requires a defined order. acceptedAt is a client clock — skew or a re-join regenerating acceptedAt could reorder bootstrap after live. The sort key for replay is implied by phase ordering, not specified as a contract.

Rule 10 (adapter outlasts engine) has no enforcement mechanism. If both live in one React provider, useEffect cleanup order is registration-order dependent, not guaranteed. Adapter torn down first -> group.off() removes applicationMessage/stateChanged before engine.stop(), starving the engine during teardown — reproducing the mountedRef guard problem (device-sync.ts:508-509) the epic aims to eliminate, now at the adapter-engine boundary.
seam_risks: Phase 3 measures the wrong seam (see BC-1). Passing Phase 3 is a false negative for state-machine correctness: joining-gate delay, live-cutover drop/reorder (syncGroup:993-1009), deferred-retry timing differences are all invisible because those paths don't run in Phase 3.

Bootstrap key collides across re-joins. appendAcceptedEvent is idempotent on event.id. On re-join, the log may retain the prior session's bootstrap entry for taskA (S1, updatedAt:1000). Re-join bootstrap fetches fresh kind-30078 reflecting S2 (updatedAt:1500) but appendAcceptedEvent SKIPS it (id exists). Engine falls back to relay kind-445 to reach S2; if those aged off the relay, task is permanently stale at S1. Bootstrap was designed for exactly this gap; the idempotency key defeats it on second join. No accepted-log reset policy on re-join is specified.

Recovery sequencing across three sources unspecified. An 'unreadable' event (device-sync.ts:739-751) has its id in raw-log AND deferred-store but NOT accepted-log, yet lastIngestedFactId IS set (processed by ingest, not accepted). On recovery: skip facts <= lastIngestedFactId -> skips the deferred event needing retry; don't skip -> re-ingest processed events. The three-way intersection replay protocol is undefined.
parallel_hazards: joining gate introduces a relay-I/O dependency the current joinBarrier lacks. Today joinBarrier resolves at MLS join completion (device-sync.ts:602) independent of relay I/O; bootstrap is called separately from task-store.tsx:115 after group load, decoupled from syncGroup. If bootstrap relay fetch (device-sync.ts:1364) hangs (no EOSE/stall), today live still opens (partial operation). Under the new gate, bootstrap must resolve before catching_up -> engine stays in joining permanently: no live, no catch-up, no projection. Today's graceful degradation becomes complete group blockage. No timeout semantics specified.

Phase 3 listener-registration window unspecified vs historical replay. Engine listener must attach BEFORE syncGroup ingests historical events (device-sync.ts:977-984) or it misses applicationMessage emitted during historical fetch. marmot-adapter.ts (registers engine listener) and syncGroup (drives historical ingest) are separate modules with no specified coordination -> false divergence from a registration race, defeating the shadow run.
evolution_triggers: Re-join after state reset is unmodeled. The joining gate is designed for first-join. On re-join (lost MLS state, new Welcome) the engine faces stale IDB: accepted-log retains prior bootstrap + accepted events. No reset policy specified (clear accepted-events vs reuse stale log with collision). The 'forget device' per-leaf flow triggers exactly this. The 'bootstrap-completed' IDB flag also interacts with the gate and has no specified fate on re-join. Undefined behavior.

spec.md:153-154 still has live links to docs/quizzl-report.md and docs/shophop-report.md (confirmed absent). The proposal removed cross-project justification from ITSELF, but spec.md is the governing doc stories are written from. The amendment is not self-applying — spec.md must be amended before stories are written.
blocking_concerns: Phase 3 cannot validate what it claims. The shadow comparison tests projection-layer accuracy only (engine state machine inactive in listener-only mode). The joining-gate, live-cutover, and deferred-retry behaviors — the novel parts — produce no signal. Phase 5 activates the state machine with no prior validation. Either redesign Phase 3 to exercise the state machine (needs an independent event stream, not shared legacy callbacks) OR explicitly scope Phase 3 as 'projection-only' and require unit-level FSM tests for receive-engine.ts before Phase 5 stories. As written it generates false confidence.

Invariant 3 weakening exists in the proposal but NOT in spec.md (still full at spec.md:663). Stories from spec.md will implement cross-epoch recovery. Either amend spec.md with the same-epoch carve-out (changes what the epic delivers) or design the epoch-keyed snapshot fork extension before Phase 2. The current split state is an implementation trap requiring an explicit decision before dispatch.

Bootstrap idempotency collision on re-join must be resolved before appendAcceptedEvent idempotency lands (Phase 2). Key bootstrap:${groupId}:${task.id} collides across re-joins; once idempotency is in place, re-join bootstrap is permanently silenced for logged tasks. A reset policy for the accepted-log on re-join, and its interaction with the bootstrap-completed IDB flag, must be specified before the PersistenceAdapter appendAcceptedEvent contract is finalized.

The engine<->adapter ingest seam must be typed before either module's stories are written. receive-engine.ts absorbs code that calls group.ingest() and client.network.subscription() directly, while marmot-adapter.ts claims to contain all marmot coupling — both cannot be true. Resolve who calls group.ingest(), who drives the subscription, and what the engine receives (raw NostrEvent[], IngestResult stream, or other) as a typed contract before independent implementation.

The joining state gate blocks catch-up on relay I/O (bootstrap fetch device-sync.ts:1364) with no timeout. Today relay unavailability degrades gracefully (bootstrap fails non-fatally, catch-up proceeds); the new gate makes it block the group entirely at joining. Specify timeout semantics and a failure-path transition (joining -> degraded or joining -> catching_up after timeout) before the joining-phase story is implementable.
